item.title: Unwilling Houdini: Re: Unwilling Houdini
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi themangoman. Let’s take a look at your concept.

I’m afraid I don’t particularly understand the concept at the moment. “Anti-containment procedures” does sound interesting, but what is an example of this? You mention:

A system of covert actions taken to make sure that the scp is on no way shape or form confined to one area due to another persons actions

But this is incredibly vague and difficult to picture. Give us a concrete example? I’m afraid I couldn’t make heads or tails or those in the table either. Which ones are accidental and which ones are attempted?

Finally, for now, tell us more about who the entity is. All you’ve listed is that it’s a “humanoid”. Give us his/her/their background. How did they get their powers? What are their goals?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Emergency broadcast system from space. Looking for greenlights: Re: Emergency broadcast system from space. Looking for greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Jungle14. Let’s take a look at your concept.

Yes, an emergency alien broadcast would be intriguing, but the entirely article cannot be based on a series of alien journal entries, can it?

The article has potential, but it’s missing details, a backstory, and potential cliffhanger conclusion. First, please tell us what the actual contents of the broadcast are. You don’t have to elaborate, but we need to know what the actual threat is. Second, I don’t understand why the scientists who made the initial discovery were amnesticised, especially if they already belonged to the Foundation? Third, okay, so after you go into detail of the four broadcasts… so what? What’s the imminent danger? What is the Foundation going to do besides waiting around?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Admin Panel: Re: Admin Panel
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Osana Akasuki. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I think you have a solid foundation. The premise is interesting, as is the potential for nifty exploration and testing logs. What I’m mainly concerned about at this point is how the article will look like, because my impression of it from reading the concept is that you’d just be listing a long page of experiments after tweaking certain settings to show various effects taking place in reality.

And then, what? You see, that’s not a coherent narrative. You have an intriguing beginning (discovery) and middle section (testing and escalation of effects), but you’re lacking an ending. It’s not enough to just say this is “God’s Program”, as I have a feeling the Foundation themselves won’t be satisfied with this answer. Was there an actual Maker of the program? If so, what were its intentions?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. All the best for now!

item.title: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
1) If the flames continue to grow then why would they stop at the edge of the city? Especially considering that there are actually more burnables there than in the center of the city? Also, how was it contained? There just seem a lot of things that are ill-defined here, and they should be better defined.

2) Speaking of: The zone of infinite place needs to be better defined. It just feels like it was added to justify the survival of the survivor and the book. If it's going to be part of the SCP, then it needs to be reasonably well-defined.

3) The bottom lines is that you've thrown so much stuff into the SCP without really defining anything that there's just nothing for a reader to grab on to, from the gauntlet to the infinite space, and the overall feel is that you're just throwing stuff at a wall hoping something will stick. Slow down, think it through, and focus on what needs to happen. Just focus on what it needs and see what happens.

item.title: Festive Jello Strikes Back: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'm largely in agreement with Grigori here; what you've got is a pretty bland monster that might have been alright on the mainsite a decade ago, but the concept as it is won't do well on the mainsite today given we have thousands of similarly dangerous entities written, many of them with more narrative to them than just "it wreaks havoc and presumably a GoI made it".

I'm also unsure about the cognitohazard/pheromone explanation, since if the jello itself is constantly secreting the pheromones, how does that trigger its own response only when "prey" is nearby? The backstory of the investigation also makes the Foundation look rather incompetent—if one field agent already went missing, why didn't the later ones take better precautions when investigating? Having a live body cam feed, radioing in their status every few minutes or so, even just sending a drone into the location to scout. It seems kind of silly that the agents' disappearance would be entirely unexplained and necessitate an MTF be sent in to do the same job.

The description of the anomaly being jello containing human remains just makes me think of the Gelatinous Cube from Dungeons & Dragons: https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Gelatinous%20Cube it also seems a little odd that it would specifically need to be festive jello; I personally don't know anyone who actually eats jello specifically for the holidays. I feel like if you really want to make this specific monster workable, you'd need to make it more distinct from the popular D&D monsters and also have an in-universe reason for why it exists the way it does. Otherwise you have something that's relatively forgettable and will be more likely compared to more interesting monsters in popular culture, rather than being interesting on its own merit.

The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

This is a big, big assumption to make here, especially since you haven't finalized what the motives of the GoI are, and it's still unclear what the point of the anomaly actually is. I myself don't really think a draft of the material currently presented would be engaging, since the core anomaly is fairly boring, the effects seem rather randomly applied and not thematically related, and the backstory is rather vague. You'd need to address all of these issues before I would think it reasonable to expect the audience to be "constantly engaged".

item.title: Mommy, Daddy, look! A rainbow!: Re: Mommy, Daddy, look! A rainbow!
item.content:encoded:
Hello jacked-anime-cole! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Eight human-looking entities created when shining a specific spotlight at a special prism.

While the premise sounds doable, there isn't enough specific information here to really get an idea of what the skip is. The concept doesn't really show what the skips motives or purpose is, or expand upon the base idea. Overall there isn't much to get invested in here as the concept is too vague.

-Some general things to expand on:

-What are these entities
-why are they important
-what is their purpose
-what part does the prism play in all of this
-why should I as the reader care about the concept? what will make me invested?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: There is none yet, but will be very soon! :)

I would highly recommend developing some sort of narrative before posting, as they help give a direction to the concept and can help with audience engagement. Articles featuring a narrative tend to favoured by modern audiences, which has more or less lead to Articles with a narrative becoming the standard. -the narrative doesn't need to be super detailed and long, short stories also work very well (it mostly comes down to execution).

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A corrosive light from a spotlight and a hazardous prism come together to shine eight colours on a wall, from Red all the way to Pink.

This feels closer to a brief summary of the skip, as there isn't much other than the skips characteristics and functions shown here. What about this will make me invested? what are the implications of this? how should this make the reader feel?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Notes:

Additional Notes: I need help with the attention grabber and the central narrative. If anyone has ideas PLEASE tell me them! Thank you!

Generally speaking, I would recommend expanding upon what you currently have. Try to get an idea on what the skips end goal is (or purpose is), and use that to get an idea on the overall narrative and central conflict.- don't be afraid to experiment with different endings or motives!

- Try to get an idea on where the narrative will start and end, that way the middle act and conflict will be easier to put together.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: The Spire - needs greenlights: The Spire - needs greenlights
item.content:encoded:
It's a chemically changing rock. Name is work in progress, and I'm not too happy with the discovery, so any help/suggestions would be nice

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/intriguing?

Page Layout (Optional): Standard article. After description, will go over discovery, and after discovery will then go over test logs.

Elevator Pitch: It's a tall rock that slightly twists. The tip of it will be called element A, and the base of it will be called element B. If an object touches the tip, element A changes into the majority of the atoms in that object. There are various things that cause a teleport event, but when that happens, the spire disappears and reappears at a random spot on the earth. element B then becomes the old element A, element A becomes the closest solid element near the tip, and the spire absorbs every current element B atom in a 1km radius.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: It was discovered when a redacted reality bender started rampaging, and along with various other items it created the spire. Some clean up MTF member accidentally touches the tip with his glove, and his glove disappears along with the spire. It's found in some town where around half of the people there dropped dead and withered on the spot, because the glove was mostly carbon, and all the carbon was stolen from their bodies. The spire is found in the town, and it's got a carbon base with a solid oxygen tip (from the oxygen in the granite that built the town)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The rules for the spire are pretty strict, so it's like a constant reminder that whatever the old tip was, all those atoms could immediately disappear in the center of a city, but it could also appear in the center of a forest, and be difficult to track down, so I feel that would draw people into the story. Also there's a mention near the beginning about testing being discontinued, so I feel people would want to see why

Additional Notes: The things that cause a teleportation event(work in progress name) are: The tip is touched with the same majority atom as the tip already had, so instead of staying the same it teleports. 108 hours pass without a tip change. If the tip is a radioactive element, the moment an atom in it decays, it undergoes the event (which is pretty much instantly). If the tip and base are the same element, it undergoes the event. If the tip is helium, it undergoes the event. I can explain more, as a lot of the info had to be cut down due to size limit.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: "Magic Horned Dragon": Re: "Magic Horned Dragon"
item.content:encoded:
Saying it like that it looks like a pokemon.

I think more mystery could be added to it. Particulary, the idea of an entity being discovered because of a epidemy looks promising but I don't think its original.

Also, if the parasite is able to make the host produces an eletromagnectic pulse wouldnt the infected people also being able to do that? Basically if each infected is capable of producing a EMP, no eletronics would work in a very big area. It could even be a global threat to take the world back to the dark ages depending on how faster the epidemy spreads. The infected are counscious of that? Or they are emmiting an EMP without knowing? A lot of information is missing.

You have some key elements here that you have to tie together: the creature, the parasite, the epidemy and the eletromagnectic pulse. What is the creature? It has a reason to look like that? If the parasite is able to preserve tissue to survive inside the creature like its alive, it could REALLY be a Prolibytherium. It could make the host emit a EMP because eletricity could be a danger to him, etc, etc.

Have a great day!
